records.name: Hive76
records.summary: A member-run makerspace where people build, tinker, and share tools. Members teach classes, and anyone can stop by a Sunday open house to see the space.
records.what_you_do: Use shared tools such as the woodshop, electronics bench, and 3D printers, take member-taught classes, and work on your own projects next to members.

schedule.text: Open house on Sundays from 2 to 5 pm.

cost.text: Light membership is $15 a month, Basic is $60, Core is $120. Member classes are free, or at cost when supplies are included.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday open house, or take out a light membership to try the space when members are around
first_step.basis: The site invites anyone to a Sunday open house and says light members can try the space, with a clear way to sign up

records.notes: Street address is from the group's own visit page. A 2011 article and an old wiki mirror give other addresses, so the visit page is treated as current. Newest dated item is a January 25, 2026 blog post.

records.name: Neighborhood Bike Works
records.summary: A community bike shop on Lancaster Avenue where neighbors work on their own bikes with the shop's tools and staff help. Youth programs teach bike repair too.
records.what_you_do: Work on your own bike at the weekly Bike Church with tools and staff help, buy ready-to-ride or used bikes and parts, or join youth programs that teach repair.

schedule.text: Bike Church on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 6:30 to 9 pm (adults 18 and older), and on the first Saturday of the month from 3 to 6 pm.

cost.text: Bike Church fees and admission are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Come to a Bike Church session. For youth programs, use the youth interest form on the site.
first_step.basis: Bike Church is a weekly open session with set times and a public address, but the site does not show adult sign-up steps or beginner notes.

records.notes: No dated news on the homepage, so status is probably_active. Youth programs have their own form and were not checked. Cost for adults is not shown.

records.name: Philly Fixers Guild
records.summary: Volunteer fixers who help neighbors repair broken household items at free pop-up Repair Fairs.
records.what_you_do: Bring a broken item to a Repair Fair and work on it with volunteers, or sign up to volunteer as a fixer.

schedule.text: Repair Fairs are listed on the group's calendar. The next two are Thursday, November 12, 2026 and Thursday, December 10, 2026, each from 6 to 8 pm.

cost.text: Free, according to the calendar listings.

first_step.how: Bring a broken item to the next Repair Fair (check the guidelines page for what is accepted), or use the Become a Fixer page to volunteer
first_step.basis: Free public events with written steps for visitors and for volunteers

records.notes: last_sign_of_life is the month of the next listed Repair Fair, from the calendar. The homepage also announces a 10th Repair Fair at Greensgrow Farms in Fishtown with no date. NextFab is a business with paid memberships and classes; only the free Repair Fair is listed here.

records.name: Liberty Bell Knitting Guild
records.summary: A knitting and fiber arts guild founded in 1987 that meets monthly in Northwest Philadelphia so members can work on projects together.
records.what_you_do: Bring a knitting or other fiber project to the monthly meeting, talk with other members, and see what they are making.

schedule.text: Meets at 11 am on the second Saturday of each month.

cost.text: Dues are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Come to the second-Saturday meeting at Cathedral Village. The site says all are welcome.
first_step.basis: An open monthly meeting with a clear time and place; no sign-up step is shown.

records.notes: The site has no dated news, so status is probably_active. Dues and visitor details were not shown.

records.name: Philly Knits
records.summary: A free fiber arts meetup for knitting, crochet, sewing, and weaving, open to every skill level, with get-togethers at rotating places and online.
records.what_you_do: Join a meetup to knit, crochet, sew, or weave with other people, in person at a rotating location or online.

schedule.text: Meetups at various locations and online. Dates are posted on the group's Meetup page.

cost.text: Free, according to the group's site.

first_step.how: Sign up through the group's Meetup page, which the group's site links to
first_step.basis: Open to all skill levels and free, with a named way to join.

records.notes: The only dated item is a September 2023 date that appears in a linked document's file name, not in an event listing. The site says the group is looking for a new Meetup organizer, so treat the status as unverified.

records.name: Philadelphia Guild of Handweavers and Fiber Artists
records.summary: A fiber arts center in Manayunk where members gather in interest groups around weaving and other fiber techniques, and where the guild runs workshops.
records.what_you_do: Join a special interest group, take part in guild programs and fall workshops, and meet other weavers and fiber artists at the Guild House.

schedule.text: Meetings and interest groups happen at the Guild House. Dates are on the group's calendar, and a 2026 fall workshop list is posted.

cost.text: Membership and class fees are not shown on the pages read.

first_step.how: Use the join page on the guild's site to become a member, then ask about its interest groups
first_step.basis: Membership comes first, and the pages read do not show a visitor option or costs.

records.notes: The homepage shows a file named for the 2026 fall workshops, dated October 8, 2026 on the page. Meeting days and public class details were not shown.

records.name: Northeast Feltmakers Guild
records.summary: A nonprofit guild for felt makers at every level. It meets on Zoom and gathers in person for a spring retreat and a few other events.
records.what_you_do: Join free Zoom meetings and workshops, take part in the spring retreat or the regional August challenge gatherings, and share felt work with other members.

schedule.text: Free Zoom meetings and workshops, plus an annual spring retreat, August regional challenge gatherings, and a November business meeting. Dates are posted on the site.

cost.text: Zoom meetings and workshops are free. Dues and in-person event costs are not shown.

first_step.how: Visit the Join Us page on the guild's site, then attend a free Zoom meeting or workshop
first_step.basis: Free online meetings and workshops are open to all, the guild says it welcomes every level, and a join page explains how to start.

records.notes: Newest dated item is an April 2026 retreat registration link. The in-person meeting place is not shown, so no location is listed. An existing data file gives a Mount Airy street address that the guild's own site did not show.

records.name: C.O.D.E. Philadelphia (Community of Developers and Engineers)
records.summary: A volunteer-run community of developers, engineers, and builders that holds weekly coding sessions and a hackathon every quarter.
records.what_you_do: Attend weekly coding sessions, join the quarterly hackathons, and meet other developers and builders. A Discord server is open for chat.

schedule.text: Weekly coding sessions, with times posted on Meetup. Recent events include an AI agent hackathon with a build day on September 20, 2026 and demos on September 22, 2026.

cost.text: Event prices are not shown. The group accepts optional donations and sponsorships.

first_step.how: Join the Discord server and RSVP on Meetup. The group's onboarding page lists these steps and says to bring a laptop.
first_step.basis: The site lays out three onboarding steps, so there is a clear way in, but it does not say beginners are the focus.

records.notes: Weekly session times and the venue are posted only on Meetup, which was not read. Venues named on the site for the September 2026 events are a build day at Pennovation Works and demos at Cesium.

records.name: Philly 2600
records.summary: A monthly open meetup for local hackers, tinkerers, and security people, held on the first Friday of the month at a Center City bookshop.
records.what_you_do: Show up on a first Friday evening to talk about tech, security, and tinkering. You can use a nickname, and no preparation is needed.

schedule.text: The first Friday of every month. People start arriving around 6 pm and stay until about 8:30 pm.

cost.text: Cost is not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Just show up on a first Friday. Bringing friends is welcome.
first_step.basis: The site says no preparation is needed and welcomes friends, with a fixed time and place.

records.notes: The site has no dated post, so status is probably_active. The www address failed a certificate check; the bare domain worked. Changes and cancellations are posted on the group's Mastodon account, which was not read. The 'hacker' label is a closest fit to the tag list; the group's security focus is in its own words.

records.name: Philly CoderDojo
records.summary: A free, volunteer-led coding club for kids ages 7 to 17. It now runs online sessions over Zoom, with volunteer mentors who help kids write code.
records.what_you_do: Kids learn programming with a volunteer mentor. Families sign up with the registration form, and adults can sign up as volunteer mentors.

schedule.text: Online dojos over Zoom. The session dates are on a Dojo Dates page that was not read. The site lists the 2025 to 2026 term.

cost.text: Free. The site says the program is completely free.

first_step.how: Families use the Dojo Registration form on the site. Adults who want to mentor use the Volunteer form.
first_step.basis: Separate sign-up forms for kids and volunteers, a free program, and a term schedule that makes it easy to start.

records.notes: The newest dated item is the 2025 to 2026 term, with no exact date, so status is probably_active. The site describes national online dojos, and it did not show in-person Philadelphia sessions.

records.name: Philly Tech Sistas
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps women of color build technical and professional skills for tech careers.
records.what_you_do: Join workshops and community events through the group's Meetup page, its Slack invite, or its newsletter to build tech and career skills with other women.

schedule.text: Workshop and meetup dates are posted on the Meetup page. The site itself shows no schedule.

cost.text: Whether events are free is not shown.

first_step.how: Use the join link to the Meetup page, or the Slack invite on the site
first_step.basis: A public group with more than one way in, though the site does not say which events suit beginners.

records.notes: No dated events on the site. The only year on the page is a 2018 footer, which is a copyright line and is not evidence, so status is probably_active on the working-site rule. Its own description names women of color, recorded here as community women.

records.name: Holmesburg Amateur Radio Club
records.summary: An amateur radio club in the Philadelphia area that meets monthly. Ham operators and curious newcomers share skills and take part in special events.
records.what_you_do: Visit a monthly meeting to learn about amateur radio, take part in club events such as the July Independence Week special event, and meet other operators.

schedule.text: Third Wednesday of the month at 7:30 pm. No meetings in June or July. The club holds a restaurant meeting in August and a Zoom meeting in September.

cost.text: Dues are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Visit a meeting, which the site says is open to all, or email the club
first_step.basis: The site says meetings are open to everyone and gives an email address; a license requirement is not shown.

records.notes: The page was updated July 6, 2026. The meeting place and license rules are not shown. Holmesburg is a Northeast Philadelphia neighborhood, and the club describes itself as serving the Philadelphia area.

records.name: Philadelphia County ARES (PCARES)
records.summary: A volunteer amateur radio group that provides emergency radio communications for the Red Cross in the Philadelphia area. No license is needed to join.
records.what_you_do: Check into the weekly radio net, train for local disasters, and help with Red Cross emergency communications over amateur radio.

schedule.text: Weekly net on Sundays at 8 pm on the Phil-Mont repeater system, 147.030 MHz, also reachable through EchoLink and ALLSTAR.

cost.text: The site mentions no dues or fees.

first_step.how: Check into the Sunday net, or follow the membership steps on the site. No amateur license is needed to join.
first_step.basis: The site says anyone interested can join with no license required; the sign-up steps are not shown.

records.notes: The newest dated item on the site is a March 2024 activation notice, so status is dormant even though a weekly net is listed. An existing data file records a 2025 date that I could not find on the site. The group covers five counties, not only the city.

records.name: University of Pennsylvania Amateur Radio Club (UPARC)
records.summary: The amateur radio club at Penn, founded in 1909 as the Wireless Club. It teaches radio and points members who want a license to study resources and exam sessions.
records.what_you_do: Fill out the club's interest form, learn about amateur radio, and get study help and exam sessions if you want to become licensed.

cost.text: Dues are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Fill out the club's interest form
first_step.basis: Membership is open to Penn alumni, faculty, staff, and students, and the page gives an interest form but no meeting details.

records.notes: Membership is limited to the Penn community (students, alumni, faculty, and staff), so it is not open to the general public. The site has no dated news, and its 2026 footer is a copyright line, not evidence. Meeting day and place are not shown.

records.name: PhillyMesh
records.summary: A Philadelphia-area group of people who experiment with mesh networking, using small radio nodes called Meshtastic and MeshCore.
records.what_you_do: Chat with local members on the group's Discord, learn to set up and flash mesh radio nodes, and try out decentralized networks.

cost.text: Cost is not shown. The site lists affiliate links to hardware and battery vendors.

first_step.how: Join the group's Discord to talk with local members, or use the Contact page
first_step.basis: An open invitation to the Discord with no meeting schedule shown, so the first step is online chat.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a September 2, 2026 post, shown in the post addresses. Meeting schedule and place are not shown. The site earns from affiliate links, which the group discloses.

records.name: Mid-Atlantic Amateur Radio Club (MARC)
records.notes: The club meets at St. Matthew's Church in Wayne, PA, outside Philadelphia. Status not scored. The home page is a frameset; the welcome page was read. An existing data file records a 2022 date that this pass did not check.

records.name: 13 Colonies Special Event
records.notes: The site describes one annual seven-day amateur radio special event station (July 1 to 7, 2026) run as a nonprofit event. It shows no membership, meetings, or sign-up for a club, so it is recorded as an event. An existing data file lists a separate association; a reviewer should check whether that club exists apart from this event.

leads_only.name: Kayuh Bicycles and Cafe
leads_only.note: Bike shop and cafe at 19th and Girard that has held free repair clinics. Clinic dates were shown without a year. Its own site was not located, so it was not checked. It is mainly a business, so it may not qualify.

leads_only.name: Northwest Philly Repair Cafe
leads_only.note: Half-day neighbor repair events that started in 2014 under Time4Time Community Exchange. Nothing found shows it still runs. Not checked further.

notes: Budget: 3 of 3 WebSearch calls used (hard cap reached), 34 WebFetch calls used. No rate limiting or 403 blocks seen. The brief asked for 25 to 50 checked records; this run has 15 publish records, 1 out_of_area and 1 not_a_group, because the making groups that were findable with three searches are mostly already in data/groups and several had no readable facts. DROPPED or NOT RECORDED: (1) PLUG, phillylinux.org: homepage newest dated entry is November 2015 and the meetings page returned 404, so no record; an existing data file covers it. (2) Code for Philly, codeforphilly.org: the site rendered only its name on three tries, so no facts were recorded; the existing data file is unverified. (3) Philly JS Club, phillyjs.com: homepage gave no meeting facts and the events page returned 404. (4) Philadelphia Furniture Workshop: paid courses ($425 to $1,425), skipped per the brief. (5) Talking Tech w/ Wayne, ttwwlabs.org: national phone and video help line; no Philadelphia meeting place shown. (6) Yellow Bicycle Collective (existing data entry): its website is a theater company, not a bike co-op, so the data entry name is misleading. Suburban model railroad clubs found in the one model railroad search, Schuylkill Valley Railroad Club (Phoenixville), Abington Lines Model Railroad Club (Richboro) and Chelten Hills Model Railroad Club (Elkins Park), are outside Philadelphia; their own sites were not located, so none were recorded. GAPS: no Philadelphia model railroad club, FIRST robotics team taking community mentors, or metalworking or blacksmithing guild was found within the search budget. Philadelphia Robotics Coalition (existing data, 1700 W Olney Ave) has no website on file and was not checked. Existing data/groups already holds many making groups not re-checked here (for example PhillyPUG, Owlhacks, The Shack Collective, Wild Geese Quilters, Philadelphia City Repair Project), which need a future pass if they have websites.
